newsitem.title: JAPAN: Large long positions weigh on TOCOM platinum.
newsitem.headline: Large long positions weigh on TOCOM platinum.

text.p: The Japanese platinum market is likely to come under pressure later this year from massive long positions held by individual investors in yen-based futures on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), Japanese traders said on Wednesday.

Traders said private investors were especially long in the December platinum contract, having been unable or unwilling to liquidate their positions when the market turned against them after rallies earlier this year.
"Technically, the massive long positions are one factor weighing on the market," a trade-house source said.
Most of the positions were built up above 1,400 yen per gram when the market rallied in January of this year and again in late March and early April.
But since early May benchmark platinum futures have rarely strayed from a 1,350 to 1,390 yen range, as the yen's weaker tone against the dollar was offset by generally weaker spot prices, they said.
Traders said private investors held long positions totalling more than 30,000 lots in the December contract, out of a total open interest of 68,855 lots as of September 17.
One factor adding to private investors' difficulty in exiting the market has been a sharp drop in trading volume in recent months, due largely to the lack of price volatility.

"If platinum futures continue to trade sideways and investors are unable to roll their positions into forward contracts, the spot December contract could fall sharply at the spot expiry later in the year, battered by heavy long-liquidation," an analyst for a commodity brokerage said.
"But private investors are tending to unleash their longs when prices approach the upper end of the ranges," he added.
